about: Review of spots_40_repaired/ (one entry per spot it repaired or flagged): keep = keep the repair; reject = apply the fix instead, from the original spot (pieces moved, dice set). 'applied' says where the fix differs from the note. proposal = a later proposed fix, reviewed on the Proposals page: proposal keep applies it, proposal reject applies the note's fix instead; the fix is always given from the original spot.

blocked_4p_021.note: Better repair: P3 dice 2 (instead of 3); P3 piece 0: square 32 -> 33; P2 piece 0: square 25 -> 24; every other piece as in the original. Reason: the automatic repair moved P3 piece 1 to 33, five squares ahead of P0's piece on 28, so it becomes exposed when it stays put (it was safe at 35 in the original). With the fix, piece 0 is still blocked (33 -> 35), piece 1 is a plain move to 37, piece 2 a plain move to 17, and every piece's exposure matches the original.

capture_4p_013.note: Better repair: P3 piece 0: 38 -> 37; P1 piece 0: 37 -> 36; P2 piece 0: 42 -> 41 (all one square back). P3's piece then sits on its last track square as in the original, cannot reach P1's piece, and P1 piece 0 still captures (36 -> 41); all moves and exposures match the original.

cvh_4p_021.note: Better repair: keep P3 piece 0: 38 -> 37, and also move P0 piece 0: 31 -> 30. Reason: with red on 31, P3's piece 0 on 37 is exactly 6 ahead and becomes exposed if P3 captures with piece 1; in the original (38 vs 31) it was 7 ahead and safe. With red on 30 the distance is 7 again, so every move and exposure matches the original.

cvh_4p_033.reason: Fails the full check: after piece 0 moves, piece 1 (square 12) cannot be captured next turn, but could originally. P1 piece 0 on square 10 reached 12 with a 2 under the original rules; under ours 12 is P1's relative 51, where P1 turns into its home column instead. Moving piece 1 and the P3 piece it captures one square back makes P1 piece 0 reach it again (a 1) and keeps the capture (11 + 5 = 16).

cvs_4p_022.reason: Fails the full check: after piece 0 moves, piece 1 (square 51) cannot be captured next turn, but could originally. P0 piece 0 on 46 reached 51 with a 5 under the original rules; 51 is P0's relative 51, where our route never stops. Piece 1 moves to 50 (P0 reaches it with a 4); the dice become 2 so piece 1 still lands on safe square 0, and piece 0 moves one back so it still captures P1 on 30.

cvs_3p_033.reason: Decoy: P1 piece 0 on square 10 looks like a threat to P2 piece 1 on 12 (a 2 under the original rules), but under ours 12 is P1's relative 51, so it turns into its home column instead. Moving P1 piece 0 and P2 piece 1 one back makes the threat real (a 2 to 11); P2 piece 0 moves two back and the dice become 2 so it still captures P1 piece 0 (7 + 2 = 9).
